## Summary

Fixed the bug in `add_business_days` by changing the weekday comparison from `<= 5` to `< 5`, which correctly excludes Saturday (weekday index 5) and ensures due dates only land on Monday through Friday.

Perfect! All tests pass. 

## Summary

**The bug was fixed by changing the comparison operator from `>` (strictly greater than) to `>=` (greater than or equal to) in the `volume_discount` function, allowing customers with a subtotal exactly at a threshold to receive the applicable volume discount.**

Perfect! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in the `to_money` function in `invoicer/money.py`, which was using `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (banker's rounding) instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP`. I fixed it by replacing the import and the rounding mode to use `ROUND_HALF_UP`, which ensures values like 2.675 and 0.125 correctly round up to 2.68 and 0.13 respectively.

## Summary

The bug has been fixed by modifying line 18 in `invoicer/csv_import.py` to strip whitespace from field names in addition to converting them to lowercase: `[name.strip().lower() for name in reader.fieldnames or []]` now properly handles CSV headers with spaces around column names.

Perfect! The fix is complete and all tests pass.

## Summary

Fixed the bug in the `is_overdue` function in `invoicer/dates.py` by changing the comparison operator from `>=` to `>`, so invoices are only flagged as overdue starting from the day after their due date, not on the due date itself.

## Summary

The bug was in the `split_gst` function in `invoicer/tax.py`. When splitting an odd tax amount like 18.01 into CGST and SGST, both halves were being independently rounded (18.01 / 2 = 9.005 rounded up to 9.01 for both), causing them to sum to 18.02 instead of 18.01.

**Fix:** Replaced the independent rounding logic with the existing `split_evenly` utility function that ensures split amounts always add up exactly to the original total by allocating any rounding remainder to the earlier parts (CGST gets 9.01, SGST gets 9.00, totaling exactly 18.01).

## Summary

Fixed the `split_evenly` function in `invoicer/money.py` by changing the condition from `i >= parts - extra` to `i < extra`, so that extra paise are now distributed to the earlier parts instead of the later parts, as specified in the docstring and tests.

The fix is complete! 

**Summary:** Added `.strip()` to the coupon code in the `apply_coupon` function to remove leading and trailing whitespace before converting to uppercase, allowing coupons pasted with spaces (like `' welcome '`) to be properly matched against the coupon dictionary.

Excellent! The fix is complete. Here's what I did:

The bug was in the `tax()` method of the `Invoice` class. The method was calculating tax on the full line amount instead of applying it to the amount after discounts. 

**The fix:** I calculated the proper ratio by dividing the discounted amount (subtotal - discount) by the original subtotal, and then applied this ratio to each line's amount before calculating tax. This ensures that tax is charged only on the discounted amount, not the full pre-discount amount.

## Summary

Fixed the EOM (End of Month) due date calculation bug by replacing the flawed logic that added 4 days to the issued date with a correct approach that calculates the first day of the next month and subtracts one day, properly handling year transitions for December invoices.

Perfect! The fix is in place. 

## Summary

The bug was in the CSV import parser which failed to normalize category names to lowercase before passing them to the tax calculation module. When a CSV line contained a category like "Reduced" (with uppercase), it would be stored as-is, but the tax calculation's RATES dictionary only has lowercase keys ("reduced"), causing a KeyError during tax calculation. The fix adds `.lower()` to convert all category names to lowercase when parsing the CSV.

Excellent! The fix is complete and working. 

## Summary

The bug was in the `format_money` function where negative amounts were displaying the negative sign twice (e.g., "-USD -12.00" instead of "-USD 12.00"). The fix was to use `abs(amount)` instead of just `amount` when formatting the monetary value, so the sign is only included once as a prefix.

Excellent! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in the `tax_for` function in `invoicer/tax.py` where it used `RATES.get(category, Decimal("0"))` to retrieve the tax rate. This silently returned zero tax for unknown categories instead of raising an error.

**Fix:** Changed `RATES.get(category, Decimal("0"))` to `RATES[category]` so that a `KeyError` is raised for misspelled or unknown tax categories, matching the documented behavior.

Excellent! All tests pass. 

**Summary:** Fixed the volume discount bug by reordering the `VOLUME_TIERS` list in descending order so that orders of 10000 and above correctly receive the 10% discount instead of the 5% discount.

## Summary

The bug was in the `parse_invoices()` function in `invoicer/csv_import.py`. The `unit_price` column was being parsed directly with `Decimal(row["unit_price"])` which failed on CSV values containing comma thousand separators (like `"1,500.00"`). The fix was to use the existing `to_money()` function which properly handles comma-formatted numbers by stripping commas before converting to Decimal.

## Summary

The intrastate GST split bug was caused by incorrect assignment of the floor division result in the `split_gst` function. The fix swaps the assignment so that `cgst` gets `tax - half` (which includes any remainder paisa) and `sgst` gets `half`, ensuring the remainder paisa is added to the first component rather than the second.

Excellent! All tests pass now.

## Summary

The bug was in the `add_business_days` function in `invoicer/dates.py`. The loop condition `while added <= days` should have been `while added < days` to correctly count the number of business days added. The off-by-one error caused the function to add one extra business day, which is why `add_business_days(friday, 1)` was returning Tuesday (2 business days later) instead of Monday (1 business day later).

The fix adds a guard clause in the `tax` method to check if the subtotal is zero and returns Decimal("0.00") early, preventing division by zero when computing the tax for an empty invoice.

**Fixed the bug by adding a zero-check in the `tax` method to return Decimal("0.00") immediately when the subtotal is zero, preventing division by zero errors on empty draft invoices.**

Perfect! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was caused by inconsistent handling of column name separators: CSV headers with underscores (e.g., `Unit_Price`) were being converted to lowercase with underscores (`unit_price`), but the code was checking for required columns with spaces (`unit price`). The fix normalizes all column names by replacing spaces with underscores during header processing and when checking for required columns, ensuring consistent matching regardless of whether headers use spaces or underscores.

Perfect! All tests pass now. 

## Summary

The bug was in the `volume_discount` function in `invoicer/discounts.py`, which was dividing the percentage by 1000 instead of 100, causing discount amounts to be 10 times too small and resulting in invoice totals being 10 times too high for qualified orders.

Perfect! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in the `statement()` method of the `Ledger` class. The running balance was being calculated using `e.amount` (which is always positive) instead of `e.signed()` (which is positive for invoices but negative for payments and credits), causing payments to be added to the running balance instead of subtracted.

Fixed by changing line 211 in `invoicer/ledger.py` from `running += e.amount` to `running += e.signed()` so that the running balance correctly decreases when a payment is recorded.

Perfect! The bug has been fixed successfully.

## Summary

The bug was in the `export_rows()` method of the `Ledger` class in `invoicer/ledger.py`. The method was incorrectly setting the `due` field to `e.on.isoformat()` (the entry date) for all entries, when it should have been using `e.due.isoformat()` (the actual due date) for invoices and an empty string `""` for payments and credit notes that have no due date.

Perfect! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in the `open_items()` method of the `Ledger` class in `invoicer/ledger.py` at line 152, where invoices were being sorted in reverse chronological order (`reverse=True`), causing payments to be applied to the newest invoice first instead of the oldest one; removing `reverse=True` from the sort fixes the FIFO (First In, First Out) payment allocation logic as documented.

Perfect! The fix is in place. The bug was in the `aging` method of the `Ledger` class in `ledger.py`, where the condition for the "1-30" bucket was using `days < 30` instead of `days <= 30`, causing invoices that are exactly 30 days overdue to be incorrectly placed in the "31-60" bucket.

Fixed the off-by-one error in the aging report by changing the condition from `days < 30` to `days <= 30` so that invoices exactly 30 days overdue are correctly placed in the "1-30" bucket instead of "31-60".

Excellent! The bug was in the `add_business_days` function in `invoicer/dates.py` where the line `current + timedelta(days=1)` was missing the assignment operator, so it wasn't actually advancing the date variable.

**Summary:** Fixed the infinite loop in `add_business_days` by assigning the result of the timedelta calculation back to the `current` variable (changed `current + timedelta(days=1)` to `current = current + timedelta(days=1)`).
Fixed the bug by correcting the `CENT` constant from `Decimal("0.1")` (which represents one-tenth) to `Decimal("0.01")` (which represents one cent).

Perfect! All tests pass now. 

**Summary of fixes:**
- Corrected the standard tax rate from 12% to 18% in `invoicer/tax.py`
- Corrected the big-order discount from 8% to 10% for orders of 10000 or more in `invoicer/discounts.py`

Fixed both bugs: increased the standard tax rate from 12% to 18% and changed the big-order discount threshold from 8% to 10%.

Excellent! The fix is complete. 

**Summary:** Fixed the late interest calculation by changing the divisor from 360 to 365 in the `late_interest` method of the Ledger class, aligning the implementation with the documented policy of calculating simple interest on a 365-day year.

Excellent! The fix is complete and all tests pass.

## Summary

The infinite loop hang was caused by a bug in the `add_business_days()` function in `invoicer/dates.py`: the function was using `timedelta(days=0)` (which doesn't advance the date) and had a `pass` statement that didn't increment the counter, creating an infinite loop; fixed by changing it to `timedelta(days=1)` and incrementing `added` when a business day is encountered.
